# Rivals bounded in time

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`rivals-bounded-in-time` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](rivals-bounded-in-time.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> A rule holding exactly within a region accepts the continuation condition's rule there and is not it where something lies outside; a rule bounded in time is such a rival, and in the clearer's witness it permits what the condition counts as a loss.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. A rule holding exactly within a region of standpoints, steps and formations is a rival wherever something lies outside it; the bounded significance is its case. (`Becoming.rival_of_outside`)
2. A significance bounded in time accepts the rule within its bound and is not the continuation condition. (`Becoming.boundedInTime`, `Becoming.bounded_in_time_rival`)
3. In the clearer's witness every formation is admitted at the first two steps; under the significance bounded at the second step the levels with the clearer's part retain what has significance, under the continuation condition they do not. (`Becoming.Clearing.admits_early`, `Becoming.Clearing.time_bounded_permits`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- No axiom; the continuation condition only as a hypothesis where stated.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- Which significance holds: every statement reading only the dynamics admits a rival, and none entails the condition where there is a standpoint and a formation (what-the-dynamics-leave-open).

**Standard boundaries:** No ethical premise and no Lean axiom is used. · Contains no ethical predicate and evaluates neither arising nor ceasing. · Stated for discrete steps. · A law of the formal model; its correspondence to actual systems is a separate obligation. · Names follow the structural naming criteria and are adopted only where the statement has their exact meaning; readings are interpretations, open to revision. · A relation omitted by a weaker description does not refute the fuller account.
